Five Apple Watch models can measure your blood pressure and alert you when hypertension may be present, but they will not provide actual blood pressure readings.

Some smart rings and other fitness devices can do this, but require periodic calibration with a traditional upper-arm blood pressure monitor. The upcoming Signal Ring claims to offer full blood pressure measurement without any calibration, citing clinical trial results involving thousands of participants...

The silent killer

Abnormally high blood pressure (hypertension) and abnormally low blood pressure (hypotension) both pose serious threats to health.

Of the two, hypertension is more dangerous, earning the nickname "silent killer" — it can cause serious and irreversible damage to arteries, the heart and the brain without obvious symptoms. Many people only discover they have the condition after suffering a heart attack or stroke.

For older adults, regular blood pressure measurement is ideal. Home upper-arm blood pressure monitors are widely available and simple to use. However, a fitness device that can be worn all day with fully automatic monitoring would be even better.

Apple Watch blood pressure features

With the launch of watchOS 26, five Apple Watch models can now measure blood pressure:

  • Apple Watch Series 11
  • Apple Watch Series 10
  • Apple Watch Series 9
  • Apple Watch Ultra 3
  • Apple Watch Ultra 2

However, these models will not provide any readings — they will only send alerts when signs of possible hypertension are detected. Other devices such as the Oura Ring work in a similar way.

Some fitness devices on the market can provide actual blood pressure readings, but require periodic calibration using readings taken from an upper-arm blood pressure monitor.

Signal Ring

Startup company Vital Signals says its Signal Ring smart ring requires no calibration yet achieves accuracy comparable to a traditional upper-arm blood pressure monitor.

CEO Tom Moss told Bloomberg that he nearly died from undiagnosed hypertension — an experience that motivated him to found the company.

The Signal Ring opens for pre-order later today, ships in October, and is priced at $399 with no subscription required. The accompanying mobile app can display real-time blood pressure readings and long-term trends (as shown in the image above).

Worth noting: the Oura Ring has not yet received approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), though clinical trials have shown it can deliver accurate blood pressure readings for thousands of participants.

Interestingly, Moss is not particularly enthusiastic about marketing the Signal Ring to all consumers. He says the feature is best suited for older adults and those assessed by doctors as being at risk of hypertension — implying that the Signal Ring may not be particularly outstanding in other areas (such as sleep tracking).
